faq.q: What is octopus ink made of?
faq.a: Octopus ink is mostly melanin, a dark pigment, mixed with mucus and other chemicals. It is stored in an ink sac and released into the water through the siphon.
A pseudomorph means false body. It is a blob of ink and mucus about the size of the octopus that hangs in the water, so the predator lunges at the fake while the real octopus escapes.
asks: Can octopus ink make a fake octopus?

faq.a: Ink may irritate a predator's eyes and can interfere with smell and taste, which many fish and eels use to hunt. Its main job is still to hide and distract.
asks: Can octopus ink blind a fish?

faq.q: How does an octopus jet away?
faq.a: It fills its body cavity, the mantle, with water and then squeezes it out hard through a funnel called the siphon. The jet of water pushes the octopus the other way, like a rocket.

faq.q: Do squid and cuttlefish squirt ink too?
faq.a: Yes. Squid and cuttlefish, the octopus's relatives, also squirt ink to escape. People have long used cuttlefish ink, called sepia, as a brown ink for writing and drawing.

facts: Octopus ink is mostly melanin, released from an ink sac through the siphon.
An ink blob held together by mucus can act as a decoy called a pseudomorph.
